name: Twenty
notes: Official docs describe workspace-specific REST and GraphQL APIs; API key is created in workspace settings and OAuth is available for external apps. Official workspace-scoped MCP supports OAuth or API key. Reviewed docs do not establish whether API credentials are available without a paid plan; access remains unclear.

name: Intercom
notes: Private apps use workspace access tokens; public apps use OAuth 2.0. Intercom documents free developer workspaces. Official hosted MCP is available only for US-hosted workspaces. Free developer workspace access should not be interpreted as free production workspace access.

name: Slack
notes: Slack platform APIs use OAuth and bot/user tokens. Official hosted MCP exists, but MCP clients must be registered Slack apps and only Marketplace-published or internal apps may use the server; workspace-admin approval and IP allowlists may also apply. API availability and MCP distribution restrictions are separate.

name: Pumble
notes: Official API addon is available on all plans and lets workspace users generate API keys. Official Pumble MCP also exists and uses credentials from a workspace addon/app; available tools depend on selected scopes. Validate the API's current endpoint coverage before estimating toolkit breadth.

name: Meta Ads
notes: Marketing API is a collection of Graph API endpoints accessed over HTTP; it is not GraphQL. OAuth-based Meta app authorization and permissions apply; advanced access/app review can be required for external use. Meta developer docs now link to MCP resources, but the reviewed sources do not establish a specific official MCP server covering Marketing API tools. Do not label MCP official without that evidence.

name: GoHighLevel
notes: Modern API authentication uses OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens; HighLevel describes PITs as static/fixed OAuth access tokens. Standard API access is documented across subscription plans, but endpoint availability is plan-dependent; the supplied sandbox reference alone does not establish a generally free developer API. Official LeadConnector/HighLevel MCP exists and uses OAuth sign-in. Access left unclear pending a precise free-sandbox/production-plan policy.

name: Shopify
notes: Shopify supports GraphQL Admin API and the legacy REST Admin API; all new public apps must use GraphQL Admin API. OAuth/token exchange is used for Admin API access; Storefront API has public/private token options. The official Shopify MCP page currently states that Shopify MCP is not publicly available yet, so this row is none for a publicly available official MCP server (not official). Developer/test stores make development self-serve, subject to platform/app rules.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
notes: SP-API uses Login with Amazon OAuth 2.0 tokens; AWS Signature Version 4 signing also applies to requests, so 'other' records that additional signing requirement. Public apps require registration and seller authorization; private developers can self-authorize. Amazon maintains an official SP-API Developer MCP sample/server. Approval and authorization requirements differ by public/private app type.

name: Fanbasis
notes: The supplied source is the product homepage, not official developer/API documentation. The x-api-key, sandbox, and free-signup claims were reportedly seen in a third-party copy and are not accepted as verified. Do not interpret blocked as proof that no API exists; it means buildability cannot be established from verified official docs.

name: MrScraper
notes: Corrected the original column shift. Official REST API uses an API token in the x-api-token header. Official hosted MCP endpoint supports OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in, with API-key fallback for clients that cannot use OAuth. The hosted MCP exposes scraperAPI, webSearch, and status. Pricing/free API credential eligibility was not established from the reviewed sources, so access remains unclear.

name: Sherlock
notes: Sherlock is a command-line username-search tool; no public web API is documented in the supplied official repository. No specific maintained official/community MCP server was established by the reviewed evidence, so MCP remains unclear rather than community. Blocked is relative to an API-toolkit build; a separate CLI wrapper is a different scope.

name: Clay
notes: Clay's Public API uses an API key; developer platform availability includes Free, Trial, and paid plans. Official MCP for Reps exists but is a separate surface from the Clay Agent Plugin/CLI. CLI runs on Mac/Linux and on Windows through WSL; API and table capabilities have plan/usage limits, and some table query features are Enterprise-only.

name: GitHub
notes: GitHub provides REST and GraphQL APIs. Authentication includes OAuth, personal access tokens sent as bearer credentials, and GitHub App JWTs for app authentication. GitHub maintains an official GitHub MCP server. Fine-grained permissions, organization policies, and rate limits still apply.

name: Neo4j
notes: This row scopes the API to Neo4j Aura API. Aura API credentials can be created on all Aura tiers; client credentials use Basic auth at the OAuth token endpoint and API calls use bearer tokens. Neo4j maintains an official MCP server for database access, which is a distinct surface from the Aura management API. Buildability is caveated because database-query operations and Aura management operations are not the same API surface.

name: Notion
notes: Internal connections and personal access tokens are bearer credentials; public integrations use OAuth 2.0. Notion hosts an official remote MCP server using OAuth 2.0 with PKCE. Connection creation permissions depend on workspace role and plan; pages/databases must be shared with the integration. The MCP server is distinct from the REST API authentication scheme.

name: Smartsheet
notes: Smartsheet REST API supports API-token bearer authentication and OAuth. Official MCP server exists, but the current MCP documentation requires Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management. Do not label access as trial without evidence that trial accounts receive API/MCP credentials and tool access.

name: Stripe
notes: Stripe API uses secret/restricted API keys and test keys. OAuth is specifically relevant to Connect platforms, not ordinary server-side API requests. Stripe's official MCP server is listed in Stripe's marketplace and connects agents to Stripe data and API operations. A developer can create test-mode keys without processing live payments.

name: Paygent Connect
notes: The supplied homepage does not establish API authentication, REST endpoints, free plan, sandbox, SDKs, or MCP availability. Claims about Authorization: Bearer pgt_live_xxx and no official MCP need first-party developer documentation. Keep this distinct from unrelated products using the Paygent name. Blocked means the build cannot be substantiated from current official evidence, not that the product definitely has no API.

name: iPayX
notes: Official FX Audit API docs describe REST endpoints, Bearer tokens, OpenAPI 3.1 and signed webhooks. Official hosted MCP is documented and listed by iPayX. However, the official pages show inconsistent free/paid pricing descriptions (including 5 lifetime free audits, 10 free audits/day, and paid developer/API plans); access is therefore unclear pending human reconciliation. MCP is confirmed official.

name: PitchBook
notes: Corrected the original column shift. PitchBook API is REST and is a separate offering requiring a standalone contract; connection is arranged through the Direct Data team. PitchBook documentation says access is established through an API key or authentication token. The supplied premium.mcp.pitchbook.com endpoint and SSO claim were not confirmed by the reviewed official API source; MCP remains unclear. A direct authentication reference for the exact PB-Token header still needs human confirmation.

name: NotebookLM
notes: Do not use the generic Gemini homepage as API evidence. Google now documents a Gemini Notebook API public preview authenticated with OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens and currently limited to personal Google Accounts. A separate Gemini Notebook Enterprise API requires an active Enterprise license and IAM role and is Pre-GA. This row uses the public-preview API mapping; confirm that it is the intended product/version for the benchmark. No official MCP server was established.

name: Otter AI
notes: Otter Public API uses Bearer API keys and is restricted to Enterprise plans with account-manager enablement. Official Otter MCP uses a separate OAuth connection and is described as available across plans; do not conflate the API plan restriction with MCP access. The API row is paid_required because the benchmark classifies API access, not MCP access.

name: Mermaid CLI
notes: Official repository documents a CLI for rendering Mermaid diagrams; it is not a public web API. No specific maintained community MCP server was established by the reviewed evidence, so do not claim community without a repository/source. Blocked applies to an API toolkit; a CLI wrapper would be a separate implementation category.

name: DealCloud
notes: DealCloud uses OAuth2 client-credentials to obtain a bearer token, with client_id and apiKey supplied to the token endpoint. API key creation depends on user-group/API permissions being enabled by an administrator; users may need an admin or Customer Success Manager. REST docs also describe Swagger/OpenAPI. No official MCP server was confirmed. Approval_required reflects admin-granted API permission, not a confirmed partner-only policy.

name: Gorgias
notes: Private apps use API keys with HTTP Basic authentication; public apps must use OAuth2 and pass app review. API credentials are available on Helpdesk plans to account owners/admins. Public app sandbox conversion from trial requires contacting Gorgias. Official Gorgias MCP exists at https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp and is available on all Helpdesk plans; this is separate from REST API auth/access.
